brief.news: Anthropic merged its Claude Cowork and standard chat products into a single unified Claude interface on September 16, 2026, and simultaneously launched two new beta tools — Claude Docs and Claude Slides — making Claude a general-purpose work environment rather than a set of separate products.
brief.story:
On September 16, 2026, Anthropic announced that Claude Cowork and Claude chat are merging into one Claude. The core change: users no longer choose which product or mode to use for a given task. Claude now determines on its own what a task requires and deploys the relevant capabilities — whether that's a quick conversational answer, a multi-step agentic workflow, document creation, or a presentation — from within a single interface.

Why the change happened
Anthropic's own announcement was candid about the reason. The company said it built Cowork for bigger projects and Design for visual work, but "people used both, and told us the frustrating part was deciding where a task belonged." Work started in one environment also didn't carry over to the other. Anthropic said it "stopped making you choose."

What is new
Alongside the merger of chat and Cowork, Anthropic launched two new tools, both in beta on paid plans:
- Claude Docs: Users create and edit documents collaboratively with Claude inside conversations.
- Claude Slides: Claude drafts presentations that users can edit directly, present from within Claude, or export as PowerPoint or PDF files.

Claude Design — a visual creation tool previously in a standalone environment — now also works inside conversations, though its standalone product continues to operate for users who prefer it.

Documents, presentations, and Design outputs live at a single shareable link accessible from a phone. Users can select individual elements or ask Claude conversationally to make changes.

How Claude handles longer work
Claude can continue working on a task after a user closes their laptop. By default, Claude asks for permission before taking an action; users can alternatively let it keep working and check in only when something needs closer attention. Users retain final say over what Claude does.

The original announcement gives a worked example: a user asks Claude to summarize what changed in a sales pipeline, write a weekly report in the team's usual style, flag items that slipped, and turn the highlights into five slides. Claude can produce both the report and the slides from the same conversation — so the slides already reflect the report's conclusions — and users can schedule the task to recur every Monday without a new prompt each time.

Existing Cowork users keep their chats, projects, artifacts, connectors, and skills where they left them. Chat users don't need to do anything differently.

Rollout
The unified experience is rolling out to Claude Pro and Max subscribers across web, desktop, and mobile over the coming weeks. Team and Free plans will follow. Enterprise administrators will receive at least 30 days' notice before the changes reach their organizations. There is nothing for Pro and Max users to turn on.

TechCrunch (Ivan Mehta) notes that Anthropic is also adding the Artifacts feature — Claude's interactive workspace — within the same unified window. Progressive Robot notes that what survives alongside the merged experience is Claude Code (the terminal/IDE product), which Anthropic kept out of scope, meaning Claude effectively goes from three front-ends to two: Claude and Claude Code.

The quote attributed to Andrew Keller, Senior Economist, in the Pulse 2.0 source also appears in Anthropic's original announcement: "I could have Claude pull up [my legal research database], and it would pull all the cases, read them, figure out which other cases I might need, download them, and store them in a folder for my personal review."

What the sources don't answer: How Keller's title connects to his use of a legal research database is not explained. The specific date Team and Free plans will receive the update is not given (Anthropic says "soon"). The source does not clarify how usage limits or billing interact with the unified model for Pro and Max users, beyond a note in mixed-news.com that "projects can reach usage limits faster" because every thread is a full Claude Code session.

sourceTexts.title: Anthropic merges Claude chat and Cowork in one interface
sourceTexts.text:
Anthropic is merging its front end for Claude chat and Cowork, making it less confusing for people to decide which tab to use for different tasks.

The unified interface lets users access chat, Cowork, and Artifacts (Claude’s interactive workspace feature) within one window. Claude Design, which was introduced in April for website and prototype design, also works anywhere within Claude.

Before this rollout, the company said customers often struggled to choose the right tab for the right task. With the new design, Claude automatically routes requests without having to switch tabs or windows. The idea is to remove confusion about which feature to pick and use just one front end to route work to different parts of the app.

Hopefully, OpenAI also takes a cue from this rollout and fixes ChatGPT’s interface across the platforms.

Image Credits:Anthropic

Anthropic is also adding dedicated features for making presentations and documents. Users can ask the AI assistant to create, edit, and present slides, and it can also download the generated presentation as a PDF or PowerPoint.

Similarly, with the Docs feature, users can work alongside Claude to create sections, ask questions, and comment on completed parts. Users can share generated documents or slides with a link and edit them on their phone.

Users can also ask Claude to start creating a document on desktop, and they can check the progress of the task using the mobile app.

These features are rolling out to Claude’s Pro and Max plans first, on the web, desktop, and mobile over the coming weeks. The company plans to extend them to the free and team tiers later.

The update comes in the wake of an upgrade of Cowork’s memory layer, which helps Claude remember user context across chats.

Sep 16, 2026

Anthropic is folding Claude Chat and Cowork into one product. Instead of switching between Chat for quick questions and Cowork for bigger tasks, Claude now figures out what a task needs on its own. Users had complained the split felt clunky, and much like the confusion around ChatGPT and ChatGPT Work, it was never obvious which environment to use since both interfaces largely overlapped.

Anthropic is also introducing Claude Docs and Claude Slides, which let users create, edit, and export documents and presentations as PowerPoint or PDF files directly in the chat. The existing Claude Design feature is now part of conversations too. Tasks keep running in the cloud when you close your laptop.

The rollout starts with Pro and Max plans. Team and Free tiers come later. Enterprise admins get at least 30 days' notice. Full details are in the Help Center.

sourceTexts.title: Anthropic is merging Claude Cowork into chat and adding Claude Docs and Slides
sourceTexts.text:
Anthropic is folding Claude Cowork into the regular Claude chat, and the merged app gets two new tools for documents and slide decks, Claude Docs and Claude Slides. The catch is timing: Anthropic's September 16 announcement says the change is rolling out to Pro and Max plans first, over the coming weeks, with Team and Free plans to "follow soon".

In the redesigned Projects, Claude suggests work it can start as parallel threads. Image: Anthropic

Anthropic says there is nothing to switch on. The update reaches existing and new Pro and Max users in the Claude app on the web, desktop and mobile as the rollout progresses, so not every subscriber has it yet. Enterprise admins will hear from Anthropic at least 30 days before anything changes for their organisations.

Anthropic ends the choice between chat and Cowork

Cowork was built as a separate place for bigger jobs, and Claude Design as the place for visual work. Anthropic says users found it frustrating to decide where a task belonged, and that work started in one did not carry over to the other.

So the split goes. Claude now works out what a task needs, and what Cowork and Design can do is available from any conversation, with the context, skills and connectors a user has set up.

Existing Cowork users keep their chats, projects, artifacts, connectors and skills where they left them. Claude Design also keeps working on its own for anyone who uses it that way.

By default, Claude asks before it takes an action. Users can change that so it keeps working and checks in only when something needs a closer look. Anthropic says Claude keeps working on a handed-over job even after the laptop is closed.

Slides can leave Claude as PowerPoint or PDF

Ask for a document and, in Anthropic's words, "you and Claude write it together". Ask for a presentation and Claude drafts the slides, which can be edited directly, presented straight from Claude, or downloaded as PowerPoint or PDF.

Docs, Slides and Claude Design are all in beta on paid plans, and Enterprise admins decide when to turn them on. Anything made with the three tools lives at one shareable link that opens on a phone, and users can select an element to move it or tell Claude what to change.

Anthropic's example is a weekly report that Claude writes as a doc and turns into five slides from the same conversation, so the numbers in both match. The report can also be scheduled to run each week without a prompt. The announcement gives no change to prices or usage limits.

Projects turn into a manager for parallel threads

A day later, on September 17, Anthropic rebuilt Claude Projects around the same hand-it-over idea. Instead of a folder of files, a project now has a coordinator that "scopes the request, delegates the work, coordinates parallel threads, reviews the outputs, and assembles the finished result."

Each thread is a Claude Code cloud session working on its own branch and copy of a repository, so two threads touching the same code end in an ordinary merge conflict. Threads share a project memory that builds up over time, and a new library collects uploaded files and the artifacts Claude produces.

Access is narrow for now. The redesign is in beta for select Pro and Max subscribers who use cloud sessions in Claude Code and have no existing projects on the web or desktop, with a waitlist for other Pro and Max users. Anthropic says more Claude Code users on those plans get access over the coming week, with projects across the rest of Claude, and Team and Enterprise plans, after that.

Anthropic warns that projects "can reach usage limits faster", because every thread is a full Claude Code session. Anyone who has watched Claude Code token bills climb on a single session will want to check the per-project usage view before starting five threads at once.

Threads run only in the cloud for now. Anthropic says running them on a user's own machine, next to local tools and code, is "coming very soon", and existing projects on Pro and Max keep working as before until the rollout reaches chat and Cowork.

Anthropic Merges Claude Chat and Cowork, and Claude Code Gains New Beta Features

September 17, 2026

Artificial Intelligence

The change is a removal, not an addition. The toggle goes away, and the routing decision moves from the user to the model.One conversation, no mode pickerBefore this week, Claude Cowork was a separate destination for larger pieces of work, while chat handled quick questions. Anthropic’s position now is that the separation was artificial: “You don’t have to choose where a task goes. Claude does more of the work.” A request typed into the ordinary message box is assessed by the model, which decides whether it warrants a short answer or a longer agentic run.The context problem the split createdThe deeper complaint was not the extra click. Work begun in one product did not carry into the other, so a user who started in chat and realised the job was bigger had to restate it. Anthropic’s summary of the fix is that “Claude can now figure out what a task needs, so what Cowork and Design can do is available from any conversation, with the context, skills and connectors you already have.”Work that outlives the sessionThe capability Claude Cowork was built around survives intact. Longer jobs continue running server-side after the user disconnects: “More involved tasks keep running in the cloud even if you close your laptop or leave the page. Come back when the task is done, and the result is waiting in the conversation.” That is the part of the old product that justified its existence, and it is now reachable from any thread.

CapabilityBefore the mergeAfter the merge

Choosing where work goesUser picks chat or Claude CoworkClaude routes the request itself

Long-running agentic tasksClaude Cowork onlyAny conversation

Visual design workClaude Design, separate surfaceInside conversations, standalone still available

Documents and decksArtifacts and the PowerPoint add-inClaude Docs and Claude Slides, in beta

Front doors to ClaudeThreeTwo

Developer terminal productClaude Code, separateClaude Code, still separate

Three collaborative surfaces ship with the merge, and all three are labelled beta on paid plans. This is the part of the announcement with the clearest competitive intent.Claude DocsClaude Docs produces a living document written jointly by the user, Claude and colleagues. Anthropic describes Claude as drafting, asking clarifying questions up front, and leaving comments explaining its choices. Documents are private by default, with Viewer and Editor access levels, and export to Word, PDF, Markdown and Google Docs. On Team and Enterprise plans they can be shared with named people, named groups or the whole organisation; on Pro and Max they are shared by link.Claude SlidesClaude Slides drafts a deck from an ordinary request. Individual slides can be edited, the deck can be presented directly from Claude, and it downloads as PowerPoint or PDF. An existing document can be converted into a presentation in place. This is a distinct product from the older Claude for PowerPoint add-in, which is worth stating plainly because the two are easy to conflate.Claude Design inside conversationsClaude Design is not new, but its location is. It now runs inside a conversation rather than as a separate destination, while the standalone version remains available for people already using it. The Next Web reports that Design is built on Canva’s design engine, integrated in April 2026; that detail comes from one outlet rather than the announcement itself, so treat it as reported rather than confirmed.What beta means here in practiceBeta is not decoration. Claude Docs is available on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans and is not available on Free. It is on by default on Pro, Max and Team, and off by default on Enterprise until an owner turns it on. Individuals can disable it under Settings, then Capabilities. It counts against the plan’s usage limits like any other work, with larger requests consuming more.

Claude Code published three substantive releases in mid-September 2026, and their contents are public. The counts below come from the project’s own changelog, not from a summary.Counting what actually shippedVersion 2.1.274 carries 108 entries, of which 13 are new additions. Version 2.1.271 carries 96 entries with 10 additions. Version 2.1.273 carries 64 entries with 4 additions. Two further releases in the window, 2.1.270 and 2.1.272, are single-line fix releases. The ratio is the story: these are maintenance-heavy releases with a small, deliberate set of new capabilities each.

The opt-in capabilities worth knowingSeveral additions are gated behind a flag or a setting, which is what makes them beta-shaped in practice. Fast mode arrived in Claude Code Remote sessions on cloud and self-hosted runners. Gateway hint headers must be switched on with an environment variable. Sessions started with remote control can now be forked, with the fork running as a background session on the user’s own machine.Controls aimed at administratorsThe other cluster is governance. Sandboxed commands gained per-command allowed domains, so the hosts a single command needs are reviewed with it and opened for that command alone. Custom and plugin subagents can be told to run without user, project and local instruction files, while managed policy files still load. Plugin installs can accept one exact command by hash instead of a blanket approval.Reading the ratio honestly
